findings.title: SUSPECT quality and empty thresholds fail-open — suppress gas/vibration safety alerts
findings.description: ingest_reading validates quality then only calls _check_thresholds when quality==GOOD. Values above configured max, or spikes >50% from the 5-minute average, are marked SUSPECT and never alert. Separately, register_sensor(thresholds={}) skips DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS (None-only fallback), so a gas/dust sensor can be registered with no warning/critical keys and never alert on any reading.
findings.impact: Life-safety / environmental monitoring disabled: toxic gas spikes, structural vibration, or dust exceedances produce no CRITICAL alerts while readings are still stored as monitoring evidence.
findings.attack_path: 1) Register GAS sensor with thresholds={} OR use defaults with max set. 2) Ingest sudden spike (e.g. 10→75 ppm) or value > max. 3) quality=SUSPECT → _check_thresholds skipped. 4) Site continues work under false 'no alerts' posture.
findings.remediation: Always evaluate thresholds regardless of quality flag (alert on BAD/SUSPECT extremes). Treat empty thresholds as DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS.get(type). Escalate SUSPECT spikes that cross critical limits.
findings.poc: value=75 recent_avg=10 max=100 critical=50 → quality=suspect alerted=False; thresholds={} → never alerts on 999

findings.title: Missing readings and TWA-only params report COMPLIANT (noise/PM fail-open)
findings.description: _get_compliance_status only inspects limits with averaging_period_hours==0. Noise/PM2.5/PM10 defaults are TWA-only (8h/24h/0.25h), so get_current_conditions always shows COMPLIANT even at 200 dBA. check_compliance skips parameters with no readings (continue), so generate_daily_report with zero data yields overall COMPLIANT.
findings.impact: Forged clean environmental compliance reports and live dashboards while OSHA/EPA noise and particulate limits are exceeded or sensors are offline.
findings.attack_path: 1) Omit submissions or stop sensors. 2) generate_daily_report → exceedances=0, compliance_status=COMPLIANT. Or submit noise=200; get_current_conditions status=compliant because no instantaneous limit is evaluated.
findings.remediation: Missing required readings → CRITICAL/unknown, not COMPLIANT. Evaluate all limit types (including TWA/short-term) in _get_compliance_status. Fail closed on sensor gaps.
findings.poc: noise 200 → compliant via instant-only check; 0 readings → daily COMPLIANT

findings.title: Crane assignment ignores capacity — overloaded lifts scheduled
findings.description: _find_available_crane returns any crane whose reach covers the zone. Equipment.capacity (tons) and DeliveryRequest.quantity are never compared. Crane schedule concurrency is also stubbed (comment admits simplified check).
findings.impact: Optimizer schedules lifts that exceed crane SWL → tip-over / dropped-load risk, colliding with concurrent bay/crane use.
findings.attack_path: 1) Register 2t crane covering Zone-A. 2) DeliveryRequest quantity=25 (tons), requires_crane=True. 3) schedule_deliveries assigns that crane. 4) Field executes overloaded lift from trusted schedule.
findings.remediation: Require delivery.quantity <= crane.capacity (with safety factor). Track crane time occupancy; reject overlapping assignments.

findings.title: get_expiring_warranties default window always empty (ACTIVE ∩ ≤90d impossible)
findings.description: status property returns EXPIRING_SOON when days_remaining≤90 and ACTIVE only when >90. get_expiring_warranties(days=90) filters status==ACTIVE AND end_date≤today+90 — empty by construction. get_summary.expiring_soon and Quick Start get_expiring_warranties(90) therefore never alert.
findings.impact: Warranties quietly expire; claims and handover miss coverage. Closeout relies on a broken alert path.
findings.attack_path: 1) Add warranties with ≤90d remaining (normal state near expiry). 2) Call get_expiring_warranties() / generate summary. 3) expiring_soon=0 despite imminent expiry → no claim filing / owner handover gap.
findings.remediation: Filter on days_remaining in (0, threshold] (include EXPIRING_SOON). Do not require ACTIVE.

findings.title: NCR contractor response auto-ACCEPTED; verify closes defects with no evidence
findings.description: record_ncr_response writes contractor text and immediately sets NCRStatus.ACCEPTED (no owner review state). verify_remediation sets VERIFIED and closes all linked defects without requiring photos, re-inspection, or hold-point clearance (distinct from already-reported hold-point skip on conduct_inspection).
findings.impact: Contractor self-clears structural/safety NCRs; defective work marked closed in QC metrics and downstream payment/closeout.
findings.attack_path: 1) NCR ISSUED for critical defect. 2) record_ncr_response(fake plan) → ACCEPTED. 3) verify_remediation(any name) → VERIFIED; defects status=closed. 4) get_quality_metrics understates open defects.
findings.remediation: Response → UNDER_REVIEW pending owner accept. verify_remediation requires linked re-inspection PASS + photo evidence; separate ACCEPTED vs VERIFIED gates.

findings.title: Forged EOT claim: attacker-controlled on_critical_path/type, empty documentation
findings.description: record_delay trusts caller-supplied on_critical_path and DelayType. calculate_time_extension_claim sums EXCUSABLE_* ∩ on_critical_path into recommended_extension. DelayEvent.documentation defaults to [] and is never required or validated against a schedule network.
findings.impact: Inflated time-extension / cost claims against owner with no evidence trail; projected_completion shifted by forged critical-path days.
findings.attack_path: 1) record_delay(..., delay_type=EXCUSABLE_COMPENSABLE, on_critical_path=True, end-start=30d). 2) calculate_time_extension_claim → recommended_extension+=30, compensable cost_impact included. 3) Export as claim basis.
findings.remediation: Derive critical-path flag from linked CPM analyzer. Require non-empty documentation for EXCUSABLE claims. Cap/validate delay_days against activity float.

findings.title: Attachment path open() arbitrary file read → SMTP exfiltration
findings.description: ConstructionEmailSender.send opens email_data['attachments'] paths with no allowlist/sandbox. Templates and Excel-driven RFI integration pass attachment lists into send(). (Subject CRLF injection is mitigated by email.header HeaderParseError on as_string; attachment read is not.)
findings.impact: Agent/workflow that sends generated mail can attach /etc/passwd, payroll, or contract files to external recipients.
findings.attack_path: 1) Set attachments=['/etc/passwd'] or relative traversal in RFI log. 2) generate_*_email → send(). 3) open() reads secret; MIMEApplication attaches; SMTP delivers off-site.
findings.remediation: Resolve paths under an attachments root; reject absolute/escaping paths. Map IDs to stored blobs instead of raw filesystem paths.

findings.title: split_csv path traversal via group_column (and slash-bearing values)
findings.description: split_csv builds filename=f"{group_column}_{value}.csv" then output_path/filename with no sanitization. Pathlib treats '/' and '..' in group_column/value as path components, writing outside output_dir (PoC: group_column='../../tmp/trav' → /tmp/trav_x.csv).
findings.impact: Malicious CSV column name/arg overwrites arbitrary writable files during 'split by category' automation.
findings.attack_path: 1) Call split_csv(df, group_column='../../tmp/trav', output_dir='/tmp/out'). 2) File written at /tmp/trav_x.csv outside intended directory.
findings.remediation: Sanitize to [A-Za-z0-9_-]; use basename only; resolve and assert filepath is under output_path.resolve().
